identity.title: Plug-and-Play Compositionality for Boosting Continual Learning with Foundation Models

problem.claim: Continual vision learners need to reduce catastrophic forgetting, especially when new tasks contain few classes.

gap.claim: Existing continual learners, including foundation-model-based methods, often recognize classes comparatively rather than compositionally and therefore remain vulnerable to forgetting.

contributions.claim: CompSLOT is presented as a universal framework for guiding concept learning across diverse continual learners.

The framework analyzes concept properties to learn semantically meaningful slots from ImageNet-pretrained vision transformers and adds primitive selection and aggregation for concept-level image understanding.
It introduces method-agnostic self-supervision that distills sample-wise concept-similarity information into the classifier to reduce reliance on incorrect or partial concepts.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CompSLOT as a universal, method-agnostic concept-level module intended to work across diverse continual learners.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments show CompSLOT significantly enhances various continual learners.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper attributes catastrophic forgetting in vision learners to comparative class recognition instead of compositional concept understanding.
It states that this limitation persists in foundation-model-based continual learners and becomes worse for few-class current tasks.
The authors introduce CompSLOT to guide concept learning across diverse continual-learning methods.
They combine slot extraction informed by concept properties, primitive selection and aggregation, and concept-similarity distillation; experiments are reported to show gains across various learners.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the failure mode, compositional concept representation, and classifier self-supervision in a single intervention pipeline.

lessons.interpretation: This alignment makes the proposed components interpretable as responses to specifically identified error sources.
lessons.application: Frame a method by mapping each module to a named failure mode, then state how the module changes the relevant representation or decision signal.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the method has no clearly separable failure modes or when module-to-problem mappings are only speculative.

unknowns: The abstract does not report benchmark names, metrics, numerical gains, baselines, or task settings for the claimed experimental improvements.
It does not specify how concept properties, primitives, or slots are operationalized, nor which continual learners were evaluated.
